claim_boundary.statement: The manifest binds the author-confirmed four-channel semantics and preserves the source drawings. It does not convert the visual construction into a G900 theorem or select a signed lift.

drawings.visual_inventory: Hand-drawn stage sequence from null through point, segment, open triangular form, closed triangular form, and a final two-face or filled-cell form.
Hand-drawn registered circular and rosette constructions using labels including i, 0, 1, x, y, z, and t.
Hand-drawn directed A-B-C turn and return construction with written procedural notes concerning motion, distance, turn, proportion, and closure.
Hand-drawn nested triangular incidence or development sketch with repeated internal subdivisions and labeled boundary points.
Hand-drawn three-arm spiral centered at i with the surrounding arms labeled x, y, z, and t.

visual_inventory: One cross-shaped registered construction is drawn.
The author identifies the left channel as a.
The author identifies the right channel as b.
The author identifies the upper channel as the ab winder.
A central fourfold oriented motif joins the channels.
The same single construction is extended downward.
The added lower arm supplies the reference channel.
Alternating oriented triangle motifs appear along the lower arm.
A rectangular enclosure is visible around part of the lower arm.
The enclosure has not yet been assigned a formal role.
The author confirms the bottom arm as the 1 channel.
The four channel roles are 1, a, b, and ab.
Rotated not-even-null endpoint symbols are marked.
The T-like bottom mark is the upside-down not-even-null symbol.
The bottom mark is not selected as a time variable.
Red circles and a red transverse line are visible but not yet formalized.

provenance_statement: The first five drawings are the preserved primary sources for the registered spiral stages. The author identifies drawings six through eight as one construction carrying the four registered channels 1, a, b, and ab.
title: Primary hand-drawing sources for the registered spiral and V4 channel synthesis
